# M20

> M20 is an educational 20 Questions-style guessing game with shared learning.

## Primary Resources

- Live application: https://m20quiz.vercel.app/
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/iamvisshu/m20-game
- Repository README: https://github.com/iamvisshu/m20-game/blob/main/README.md

## What M20 Is

M20 is a browser-based guessing game inspired by the classic Twenty Questions format and modern 20Q-style guessing systems.

A player thinks of something and answers a sequence of questions. M20 uses those answers to rank candidate entities and eventually attempts to guess the player's concept.

M20 uses five answer states:

- YES
- PROBABLY YES
- UNKNOWN
- PROBABLY NO
- NO

## Core Architecture

M20 is built with:

- React
- TypeScript
- Vite
- Supabase
- PostgreSQL
- Supabase Auth
- PostgreSQL Row Level Security
- PostgreSQL RPC functions
- Vercel

The frontend contains separate layers for:

- UI
- application/game service logic
- domain models
- game engine
- repositories
- shared libraries

## Game Engine

The engine uses:

- candidate scoring
- information-gain based question selection
- confidence thresholds
- score-gap thresholds
- maximum question limits
- early guessing

The engine is designed to be independently testable and simulatable without depending on the browser UI.

## Knowledge Model

Core concepts include:

- Entity
- Attribute
- Question
- Answer
- Evidence
- Confidence
- Candidate

Entities are associated with attributes and categories.

Questions are associated with attributes.

Gameplay answers produce evidence that can be used by the learning system.

## Learning System

M20 uses anonymous gameplay evidence to improve shared knowledge.

Learning updates are evidence-based and designed to avoid allowing a single incorrect answer to immediately corrupt global knowledge.

The learning model includes:

- evidence
- entity attribute statistics
- knowledge history

## Database

Primary reference tables:

- categories
- entities
- entity_categories
- attributes
- entity_attributes
- question_families
- questions
- entity_aliases

Gameplay tables:

- games
- game_questions
- game_answers

Learning tables:

- evidence
- entity_attribute_stats
- knowledge_history

## Security

M20 uses PostgreSQL Row Level Security.

Protected gameplay and learning mutations are handled through secured database RPC functions.

Privileged Supabase service-role credentials must never be exposed to the frontend.

Anonymous authentication is used for gameplay sessions.

## Categories

Current gameplay categories include:

- Everything
- Animals
- Everyday Objects
- Food & Drinks
- Household
- Technology
- Vehicles

## Entity Aliases

M20 supports normalized aliases for entities.

Examples:

- Television → TV
- Refrigerator → Fridge
- Motorcycle → Motorbike
- Airplane → Aeroplane

Aliases resolve to canonical entities.

## Testing

The repository contains:

- unit tests
- integration tests
- E2E tests
- game simulations

Simulation metrics include:

- accuracy
- average questions
- median questions
- maximum questions
- early guessing
- unanswered games
- incorrect guesses
- confidence
- score gap
- effectiveness

## Local Development

Repository:

https://github.com/iamvisshu/m20-game

Local path used by the developer:

/Users/iamvisshu/Documents/GitHub/m20-game

Install dependencies:

npm install

Start development server:

npm run dev

Build:

npm run build

Supabase migration status:

npx supabase migration list

Push Supabase migrations:

npx supabase db push

## Environment Variables

The frontend requires:

VITE_SUPABASE_URL
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY

Do not expose service-role credentials.

## Project Philosophy

M20 is intended as an educational, production-minded demonstration of:

- interactive game architecture
- knowledge representation
- information theory
- candidate ranking
- uncertainty handling
- evidence-based learning
- PostgreSQL data modeling
- database security
- concurrent learning updates
- frontend engineering

M20 collects minimal personal information and does not require a traditional user account.
